summary: Shi Wang specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Wang earned a BA at Yale University (2020–2024) and studied for a DPhil at the University of Oxford (2024–2025).

Shichang Ma was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Ma worked at the Dunhuang Academy as a researcher in Buddhist archaeology (1963–1978) and joined Peking University's Archaeology Department in 1982, teaching Giuseppe Vignato.
Shigeki Kaizuka worked in sinology, history, and archaeology. After studying at Kyoto University (~1925–1928), he held a post there from circa 1947 to 1968.

Shigeki Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant at Kyoto University, an associate professor at Shuchiin University, and an associate professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1972–1973).

Shigeki Moro specializes in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and philosophy. He studied at Waseda University, Toyo University under Ryoshun Okubo and Koyu Tamura, and Kansai University. He served as professor at Hanazono University (2002–2025) and Waseda University (2025).
Shigemasa Fukui is a sinology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Waseda University (~1954–1964) and later served as a professor there from circa 1980 to 2006.

Shigemitsu Dando studied at the University of Tokyo under Seiichiro Ono (~1932–1935). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), Keio University, and the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983).

Shigenori Nagatomo works in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Temple University, including as professor of religious studies (attested 1999 and 2017), and taught Kin Cheung and Tao Jiang.

Shigeo Kamata was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Kodo Sawaki and earned doctorates at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo, Matsugaoka Bunko, and Aichi Gakuin University (~1988–1998).

Shigeo Yokoyama studied at Kyoto University (~1973–1982). A scholar in religious studies and other fields, he held academic posts at Okayama University (~1984–1994) and Nara Women's University (~1994–2019).

Shigeru Gorai worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, and held posts at Koyasan University, Otani University (1955–1978), and the Institute of Japanese Religious Folklore (1974–1993).
Shigeru Kato was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1906) and later held an academic post there from circa 1925 to 1941.

Shigeru Matsumoto was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1959) and Harvard University (~1962–1967). He held posts at Tenri University (~1968–1980) and the University of the Sacred Heart (~1980–2003).
Shih-Hsiang Chen was a sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1931–1935). He held a post at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1945 to 1971, where he taught Gary Snyder.

Shikaripur N. Sridhar works in linguistics and Indology. He has held multiple roles at Stony Brook University, serving as Chair (attested 2007) and as SUNY Distinguished Service Professor and Director of the Center for India Studies (attested 2016, 2026).
Shikazo Mori was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1926 to 1929 and later held a post at Bukkyo University (~1970–1980).

Shikha Rajpurohit works in Indology and philosophy. She studied Sanskrit at Lady Shri Ram College for Women (2009–2012) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (2014–2022), and was appointed assistant professor at Krea University in 2024.

Shili Xiong was a philosopher and scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied under Jian Ouyang at the China Institute of Inner Learning in 1920 and held posts at Peking University (1923–1955), Boone University, and Zhejiang University (~1942–1944).

Shilpa Sumant is an Indologist who earned a Ph.D. at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (2000–2007). She held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (2009) and the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2020–2025).

Shimei Futabatei was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at Senshu College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Hitotsubashi University. He taught at the Army War College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Naval War College.
